scope: Twenty-six consecutive years, the whole civil series from its first volume, read for a Mazza groom.
result: EXACTLY ONE in twenty-six years: Mariano Mazza, act 17 of 1836, to Agata Catalano of Macchia, «figlio di IGNAZIO e di GIUSEPPA PULVIRENTI». scope: Four years read ENTIRE — over five hundred births — for brothers and sisters of Rosario Mazza.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1854, act located by arithmetic
scope: The 1854 Tavola carries no act numbers. Two acts to an opening, act = 66 + 2×(image−36), which puts late April at images 39–41.
result: ACT 76. Giovanni Arena born 30 April 1854, declared by his grandfather GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, 75, marinaro, «figlio del fu DOMENICO». The Tavola said «Rosa Arlotta» and 20 April and was wrong twice. Giovanni Arena is Rocco's FULL BROTHER, and DOMENICO ARLOTTA is the deepest name on the Calabrian side.

scope: The corrected coverage note opened forty-eight volumes. 1885 for the Arena weddings; 1888 for Rocco Arena's own.
result: THREE ACTS. 1885 atto 73 and atto 86: two of Rocco's brothers married seven weeks apart. 1888 atto 63: ROCCO ARENA'S OWN MARRIAGE ACT names his parents outright — Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta — and gives Generosa Costa's parents for the first time, Antonio Costa and ANNA ARLOTTA.

scope: The 1888 marriage index is destroyed by water across exactly the A entries. The BANNS are a separate series of 46 volumes with their own annual index.
result: THE WAY ROUND A DESTROYED INDEX. Publication 63, 18 November 1888: Francesco Antonio Arena appears IN PERSON, alive, sixty-eight, a pescatore, a week short of sixty-nine. And the couple swore there was no impediment of kinship — so Rocco and Generosa were NOT first cousins.

scope: The year nobody had read. The archive had read 1851 (the tree's date), 1856 and 1859 (a declared age) and closed the search.
result: MICHELE DONATO, BORN 3 OCTOBER 1855, act 163 — «DOMENICO DONATO, figlio di CANDELORO, trentotto, marinaro» and «NUNZIATA SOFI, trentasette». Three generations in one act, the ages exact at both ends, and the longest open question in the archive answered.

scope: Eighty-one volumes of deaths, 1866–1943, that this archive did not know existed. The annual index carries a PATRONYMIC as well as a name.

But three acts found: Fortunato Arena (ten days old, Via Grotte 70), Maria Donato (twenty-eight months, Via Grotte 21) and Orazio Arena — who turns out NOT to be the tree's Orazio.

And 1843 act 11 shows a DONATO ANTONIO «figlio di BRUNO»: there are at least TWO Donato lines in the town, which is why the Donato marriages of the 1870s are numerous and none is his.

scope: PROSTAMO, MELLUSO, ANILE, VENTRICE, ARLOTTA searched across all Geneanet record sets (trees, archives, transcriptions).

PROSTAMO returns eight entries, every one a New Haven or Hamden, Connecticut vital record 1914-1955 — an American cluster of the surname, untested against Briatico and claimed as nothing. MELLUSO (506) is an Agrigento family. VENTRICE (730) is Ustica and French Algeria. ARLOTTA (881) is Buffalo, New York. scope: Searched the register index on localita=Potenzoni after three straight years of Briatico births turned up no Prostamo at all.
result: POTENZONI IS ITS OWN COMUNE ON ANTENATI, WITH 57 REGISTERS. It is a frazione of Briatico and it kept its own civil register from 1806. Everything read at Briatico so far has been the wrong parish if the family lived there. Births 1812-1837 are a single 364-image volume; marriages 1812-1858 a single 293-image volume; and the marriage allegati 1812-1850 hold the spouses' own birth certificates. This is the largest unopened door in the Calabrian half of the archive.

source: Antenati — Potenzoni, Nati: the volume opened and mapped
scope: an_ua37927182 / container 0AQJBAW, 364 images. Located the annual blocks: fourteen images to a year, two acts to an opening, each year closed by a Rubrica listing every birth in date order. 1818 index at image 66, 1819 at 80, 1820 at 104-106.
result: PARTIAL. Potenzoni 1818 read in full (entries 12-21) and 1820 read in part (entries 7-16 of 23). No Prostamo in either. Two cautions recorded for whoever continues: the photographer left the 1819 Tavola and a title sheet lying on top of EVERY frame in this run, so the printed year visible at the head of an image is not the year of the page beneath it; and the volume is not purely Potenzoni — the register bound in at image 106 is headed «Comune di Briatico», for 1822, which suggests these are the second originals deposited with the tribunal and that Briatico years sit inside the Potenzoni unit.

scope: Keyword PROSTAMO across newspapers, gazettes, books, archives and people.

Three named Brisbane Prostamo with street addresses and exact dates — new to this archive, and untested against the line.

scope: The same keyword against the digitised Queensland newspapers, and PROSTAMO + funeral.
result: NEGATIVE. Not one Prostamo appears in a digitised Australian newspaper before 1961, and Domenica Prostamo's death on 3 May 1928 produced no notice that Trove holds. Weak evidence on its own — ordinary families rarely reach print — but it means the Brisbane newspapers will not date this family's arrival.

source: Queensland BDM — the historical index, by download
scope: The registrar's own downloadSearch endpoint returns the full result set as CSV, which makes an exact-surname sweep of births 1829-1926, marriages 1829-1951 and deaths 1829-1996 a single request per name. Prostamo, Postamo, Melluso, Limardo, Borello, Polistena.
result: One Prostamo in the whole index: Maria Assunta, died 27 October 1991, born 1936, parents Gregorio Melluso and Carmela Maria Borello. One Melluso: Gregorio, died 30 September 1971, parents Gennaro Melluso and Maria Limardo. Postamo, Limardo and Polistena return nothing at all. result: Plots 607 and 608 are known. The adjoining plots on either side are not, and at Nudgee it was the neighbouring plots that joined families to each other.

scope: Every page of every volume read by cropping the parroco's certificate box, which names both spouses, and montaging them.
result: THE MARRIAGE WAS FOUND. Briatico 1849 ATTO 1, 14 June: DOMENICO PROSTAMO marries GIOVANNA VENTRICE. Thirteen years of Briatico marriages were read to reach it — 1840 to 1848 hold no Prostamo at all, and neither do 1850, 1851, 1852 or 1854, read earlier. The act names ANTONINO PROSTAMO and MARIA FRAGALÀ, and says Domenico was born at PIZZO.

scope: Domenico Prostamo was born at Pizzo about 1813; his mother Maria Fragalà was still living there in 1849; and the family tree puts his grandfather Pasquale's death at Pizzo on 4 January 1829.
result: THE FAMILY IS A PIZZO FAMILY, NOT A BRIATICO ONE. Every hour spent on Briatico births and on Potenzoni was spent in the wrong comune. Pizzo's own registers at the Archivio di Stato di Catanzaro have not been opened once.

scope: The processetti filed with atto 1 of 1849.
result: The act says the groom produced his father's AND his paternal grandfather's death certificates, and the bride hers. Four death records and probably two birth records are sitting in that bundle, and they would date Antonino Prostamo's death and reach the third generation.

scope: Opened on the reasoning that three Prostamo-free years of Briatico births meant the family was in the frazione.
result: THE REASONING WAS WRONG AND THE NEGATIVE WAS RIGHT. They were not at Potenzoni either; they were at Pizzo. Recorded because the mistake is instructive: an absence was read as evidence for a specific alternative rather than as evidence of absence, and the right move would have been to find a document that says where they were — which is what the marriage act eventually did. The Potenzoni mapping is kept; it is good work on a comune this family does not appear to belong to.
